title: Methodology and law
description: Before any tool runs, a penetration test is defined on paper and bounded by law. This module covers the recognised methodologies (PTES, OSSTMM and NIST SP 800-115), the authorisation letter, scope and rules of engagement that make a test lawful and safe, the Indian legal framework (IT Act 2000, CERT-In Directions, DPDP Act 2023), and the evidence, lab-safety and reporting disciplines that make the work trustworthy and useful.

lessons.title: PTES and OSSTMM overview
lessons.summary: How the PTES seven-phase lifecycle, the OSSTMM measurement approach and NIST SP 800-115's four phases give a penetration test structure, repeatability and coverage.
objectives: Describe the seven PTES phases and the output each phase hands to the next
Explain OSSTMM's channels, porosity and operational controls and why it measures rather than lists
Map PTES and OSSTMM onto the NIST SP 800-115 four-phase model and its feedback loop
Choose and justify a methodology spine for a given engagement

lessons.title: Authorization letter
lessons.summary: What a written authorisation to test must contain, who can validly sign it, and how third parties and contracts fit around it.
objectives: Identify the mandatory elements of an authorisation letter
Determine who has authority to authorise testing of a given asset
Explain why cloud, hosting and other third-party providers need separate consent
Relate the authorisation letter to the MSA, SOW and NDA that surround it

lessons.title: Scope
lessons.summary: How to define precisely what may and may not be tested, verify ownership of every target, and handle assets discovered during the test.
objectives: Write a scope that lists in-scope targets precisely and out-of-scope items explicitly
Verify that the client owns or controls every in-scope asset
Apply a stop-and-ask decision procedure to newly discovered assets
Distinguish black-box, grey-box and white-box scoping and their trade-offs

lessons.title: Rules of engagement
lessons.summary: How rules of engagement govern the conduct of a test: permitted techniques, windows, communication, escalation and stop conditions.
objectives: List the core sections of a rules-of-engagement document
Define stop conditions and the escalation path for critical findings
Explain how source addresses, test windows and notifications let defenders tell a test from an attack
Draft rules of engagement for the course lab

lessons.title: Legal boundaries in India
lessons.summary: The Indian legal framework that bounds penetration testing: IT Act 2000 sections 43, 66, 70 and 72A, the CERT-In Directions of 2022 and the DPDP Act 2023.
objectives: Explain how IT Act section 43 creates civil liability and section 66 makes the same acts an offence
Identify when protected-system, confidentiality and extraterritorial provisions apply
Describe CERT-In's role and the reporting duties in its 2022 Directions
Apply data-protection duties under the DPDP Act 2023 to data met during a test

lessons.title: Evidence handling
lessons.summary: How to capture reproducible, timestamped evidence, protect its integrity with hashes, and keep a chain of custody from capture to destruction.
objectives: Capture evidence that lets another tester reproduce a finding
Compute and verify SHA-256 hashes of evidence files
Maintain a chain-of-custody record across hand-offs
Apply minimisation, retention and destruction rules to sensitive evidence

lessons.title: Lab safety
lessons.summary: How to build and run a practice lab that cannot reach anyone else's systems, using isolation, snapshots, loopback binding and tool-level scope checks.
objectives: Design an isolated lab topology using host-only or internal networking
Explain how loopback binding and allowlists enforce scope in code
Use snapshots, separation of tools and data, and cleanup to keep the lab safe
Run the course lab's scope refusal and interpret its result

lessons.title: Report templates
lessons.summary: The structure of a professional penetration-test report, the anatomy of a finding, and how the lab pipeline turns verified evidence into a ranked, retestable report.
objectives: Describe the sections of a penetration-test report and their audiences
Write a complete finding entry with evidence, CVSS vector, impact and remediation
Trace the lab pipeline from verification to report to retest
Review a report against a quality checklist before release
